A "B" team, consisting of Boddington, Clark, Cornish, Martin, Snell, Reeve and Sutton also started. From the start our walkers were prominent, together with those of Surrey W.C. and Leicester W.C.—the three teams securing the placings in last year's race.

Our "B" team (Clark, Doubleday, Roberts and True) managed to get in the prize-winners again, taking second handicap team prize. Brunning, Jones and Little also gave us encouraging performances, and their constant support of open races is an excellent testimony to their keenness and club-spirit.
Roberts, Doubleday, Clark and Heather, of the "B" team, walked well and comprised the second handicap team. Eddie Heather's forward walking, his best to date, earned third individual handicap prize.

This was held at Wimbledon on October 24th jointly with a match against Herne Hill H. and Sutton and Cheam Harriers. Maynard, Clark and Heywood were the first three home, followed by Chas, Walker and P.
Maynard and Clark in the lead found their way over strange ground without difficulty. Charlie Walker was running well to come 3rd and Cliff Roffey 4th.

The eighth leg was run by Bedford who was only too pleased to run whereever the selectors decided and though he lost places to Norris and Clark he still gave a sterling performance and established a new club best by 10 seconds.

The last heat gave John Davis a chance to show his paces, but Clark of Aylesbury opened a big gap in the third lap and before John could extricate himself from the rest of the field, Clark was too far away.
Baulch especially was in fine fettle to finish 11th behind such names as Firth, Caulder, Barrett, Towl, Maynard, Clark and Driver, all of whom are in international class in one sphere or another.

From this point he fell back steadily and at the finish was seven minutes behind the winner, Clark of Herne Hill. The fact that we could only scrape third place in the team race was mainly due to A.Bishop running some fourteen minutes slower than he did last year.
That man from the "Green Belt", Ray Middleton, walked his usual fine race to finish 4th (79.01) behind Clark (Poly.) 76.07, D. Thompson (Met.) 76.11, and Godbeer (Camb.) 76.23.
George Williams took the lead at 2 miles in 14:47 and was leading Clark by 11 secs. at 3 miles. In the next mile, however, Clark cut down this lead and was 1 sec. ahead of the Belgravian at 6 miles.
